extra_vocab.zh: 被捲入、深陷（caught up in）；趕上；抓住
extra_vocab.en: past form of catch; in "caught up in", it means so busy or involved in something that it is hard to stop
extra_vocab.note: 在文章裡是 be caught up in（深陷於…）的 caught，表示人被日常責任綁住、停不下來，語感帶一點無奈。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: catch 是不規則動詞：catch–caught–caught，不是 catched。be／get caught up in 後面接名詞或 V-ing，表示被動地陷入。

example.en: She catches the 7:30 train to the Taipei office every morning.
example.zh: 她每天早上搭 7:30 的火車去台北辦公室。

example.en: We are catching a flight to Tokyo for the sales meeting.
example.zh: 我們要搭飛機去東京參加業務會議。

example.en: Please wait here while I catch up with the sales team.
example.zh: 我去追上業務團隊，請在這裡等一下。

example.en: I need two hours to catch up on unread emails.
example.zh: 我需要兩小時處理未讀的電子郵件。

example.en: The new logo caught the customers' attention right away.
example.zh: 新標誌立刻吸引了顧客的注意。

example.en: We must leave early to catch the 6 a.m. flight.
example.zh: 我們得早點出發才趕得上早上六點的班機。

examples.en: Many managers get caught up in daily tasks and forget long-term plans.
examples.zh: 許多主管被日常工作纏住，忘了長期計畫。

examples.en: Sorry for the late reply. I was caught up in a client meeting.
examples.zh: 抱歉這麼晚回覆，我剛被客戶會議絆住了。

examples.en: The team was caught in the rain on the way to the factory.
examples.zh: 團隊在前往工廠的路上遇到下雨。

examples.en: After the holiday, it took us a week to get caught up.
examples.zh: 假期後，我們花了一週才趕上進度。

confusable.diff: taught 是 teach（教）的過去式；caught 是 catch 的過去式，兩個字拼法和發音都很像。

example.en: Our manager taught us how to handle difficult customers.
example.zh: 我們的經理教我們如何應付難搞的客戶。

confusable.diff: court 是名詞，指法院；caught 是動詞，發音相近但意思完全不同。

example.en: The company will take the case to court next month.
example.zh: 公司下個月會把這個案子告上法院。

example.en: Please grab a seat and wait for the manager.
example.zh: 請找個位子坐下，等經理過來。

example.en: The ad captured the attention of many young buyers.
example.zh: 這則廣告吸引了許多年輕買家的注意。

example.en: Heavy rain trapped dozens of travelers at the airport.
example.zh: 大雨把數十位旅客困在機場。

derived.link: catch + -y，像 sunny、rainy 變成形容詞；容易「抓住」人耳朵的

example.en: The auditor caught a mistake in the quarterly report.
example.zh: 稽核員發現季報中有一個錯誤。

example.en: The price looks low, but there is a catch.
example.zh: 價格看起來很低，但其中有陷阱。

senses.en: to become so involved in something that you cannot easily stop

example.en: The team got caught up in a long argument about the budget.
example.zh: 團隊陷入一場關於預算的長時間爭論。

senses.en: to get on a bus, train or flight in time
senses.distinguish: 受詞是交通工具或班次時，就是趕搭的意思。

example.en: We have to hurry to catch the last train home.
example.zh: 我們得趕緊搭上回家的最後一班火車。

senses.distinguish: 受詞是 a cold、the flu 等疾病時用這個意思。

example.en: He caught a cold during the business trip.
example.zh: 他在出差期間感冒了。

senses.en: to hear or understand what someone says
senses.distinguish: 受詞是別人說的話或名字時用這個意思。

example.en: Sorry, I didn't catch your name. Could you repeat it?
example.zh: 抱歉，我沒聽清楚你的名字，可以再說一次嗎？

extra_vocab.en: a fight between companies to sell at lower and lower prices
extra_vocab.note: 例句的 got caught up in 是「被捲入」的意思；price war 帶負面語氣，因為各家公司降價後都賺得更少。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: price war 是可數名詞，常說 a price war、in a price war；「被捲入」用 get caught up in，不是 get caught on。

examples.en: The two airlines started a price war on short flights.
examples.zh: 兩家航空公司在短程航線上展開價格戰。

examples.en: We should avoid a price war and focus on service quality.
examples.zh: 我們應該避免價格戰，把重點放在服務品質。

examples.en: A price war could cut our profit by half this year.
examples.zh: 價格戰可能讓我們今年的利潤減半。

examples.en: Shoppers benefit when two supermarkets begin a price war.
examples.zh: 兩家超市開打價格戰時，購物者就受惠了。

similar.diff: price competition 較中性，只是比價格；price war 強調激烈對抗，降價到影響獲利。

example.en: Price competition in this market is getting stronger every year.
example.zh: 這個市場的價格競爭一年比一年激烈。

similar.diff: price cutting 是降價這個動作，可以是單方面；price war 是雙方互相降價。

example.en: Heavy price cutting hurt the profits of the whole industry.
example.zh: 大幅降價傷害了整個產業的利潤。

confusable.diff: trade war 是國家之間用關稅等手段互相打擊；price war 是公司之間比誰賣得便宜。

example.en: The trade war raised the cost of imported steel.
example.zh: 貿易戰推高了進口鋼鐵的成本。

confusable.diff: bidding war 是買家互相搶著出高價；price war 是賣家互相降價。

example.en: Three buyers started a bidding war for the old factory.
example.zh: 三位買家為了那間舊工廠展開搶標戰。

extra_vocab.zh: 我都處理完了（我已經趕上進度了）。
extra_vocab.note: 回覆同事或主管時的口語說法，表示「積壓的事都處理完了」。注意這裡的 caught up 與文章中 get caught up in（被捲入）意思不同。
extra_vocab.structure: S + be + all + caught up（過去分詞當形容詞）

grammar.explain: be caught up 是過去分詞當形容詞，表示已趕上進度、沒有積壓的事；後面可接 on + 事情或 with + 人／事。
all 放在 be 動詞後、形容詞前，表示「完全、全部都」，語氣比 I'm caught up 更肯定。

grammar.point: caught up on／with 與 caught up in 不同
grammar.explain: caught up on／with 是「補完、趕上」；get caught up in 是「被捲入、深陷」，介系詞不同，意思差很多。

extra_vocab.pattern: I'm all caught up (on + 事情)

paraphrase.en: I have finished everything I was behind on.
paraphrase.zh: 我已經做完所有落後的事了。

paraphrase.en: I've caught up on all my work.
paraphrase.zh: 我已經把所有工作都補上了。

examples.en: Thanks for waiting. We're all caught up on this month's orders.
examples.zh: 謝謝等候，本月的訂單我們都處理完了。

examples.en: She is all caught up with her emails after the trip.
examples.zh: 出差回來後，她已經把電子郵件都回完了。

key_words.zh: 趕上進度、處理完積壓的事

extra_vocab.en: giving all your attention to something
extra_vocab.note: 和文章的 caught up in 意思接近，都有「投入其中」的感覺；absorbed in 偏正面，指全神貫注、忘了周圍，caught up in 常有被事情拖著走的感覺。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: absorbed in 的 in 是介系詞，後面接名詞或 V-ing；主詞通常是人，不是事情。

examples.en: She was so absorbed in the data that she missed lunch.
examples.zh: 她太專心看數據，連午餐都錯過了。

examples.en: Everyone was absorbed in the presentation for an hour.
examples.zh: 大家專心聽簡報聽了一個小時。

examples.en: He gets absorbed in his English practice every evening.
examples.zh: 他每天晚上都全神貫注地練習英文。

similar.diff: immersed in 強調整個人泡在某個環境或活動裡，程度更深。

example.en: The new staff are immersed in training this week.
example.zh: 新進員工這週完全投入訓練。

similar.diff: focused on 強調把注意力放在目標上，不一定忘了周圍。

example.en: We stay focused on customer needs during every project.
example.zh: 每個專案中，我們都專注於客戶需求。

confusable.diff: absorbed into 是被併入、被吸收進某個團體；absorbed in 是專注於某件事。
confusable.usage: be absorbed in 的主詞是人，表示專心；be absorbed into 的主詞多是公司或部門，表示被併入。

example.en: The small shop was absorbed into a larger retail group.
example.zh: 那家小店被併入一個較大的零售集團。

extra_vocab.en: all the time, or again and again
extra_vocab.note: 文章中的 constantly strive 表示人們不停地努力追求更多，帶有停不下來、有點疲憊的語氣。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: constantly 常放在動詞前（constantly changing）或 be 動詞之後；搭配進行式時有「一直在…」的抱怨語氣，如 He is constantly late。

example.en: The market is constantly changing, so we update prices weekly.
example.zh: 市場不斷變化，所以我們每週更新價格。

example.en: We constantly update the product list on our website.
example.zh: 我們不斷更新網站上的產品清單。

example.en: Our goal is to constantly improve our delivery time.
example.zh: 我們的目標是不斷縮短送貨時間。

examples.en: Our competitors constantly lower their prices to win more customers.
examples.zh: 我們的競爭對手不斷降價來爭取更多客戶。

examples.en: Sorry for the delay. The server has been constantly crashing today.
examples.zh: 抱歉延誤，伺服器今天一直當機。

examples.en: He constantly arrives late, so his manager spoke to him.
examples.zh: 他經常遲到，所以經理找他談過。

examples.en: Flight schedules constantly change during the busy holiday season.
examples.zh: 旺季假期期間，航班時間經常變動。

confusable.diff: consistently 是「一貫地、穩定地」，強調每次都一樣；constantly 是「不斷地」，強調頻率高。

example.en: She consistently meets her sales targets every quarter.
example.zh: 她每一季都穩定達成銷售目標。

confusable.diff: continuously 是中間完全不中斷地持續；constantly 可以是一再重複發生。

example.en: The machine ran continuously for twelve hours without a break.
example.zh: 這台機器連續運轉十二小時沒有休息。

confusable.diff: instantly 是「立刻、馬上」，constantly 是「不斷地」，字尾相似但意思不同。

example.en: The software instantly sends a receipt to the customer.
example.zh: 這個軟體會立刻寄收據給客戶。

similar.diff: all the time 較口語，通常放在句尾；constantly 較正式，放在動詞前。

example.en: The printer breaks down all the time in our office.
example.zh: 我們辦公室的印表機老是壞掉。

similar.diff: always 多用在習慣，語氣中性；constantly 常帶「一直重複、有點煩」的感覺。

example.en: She always checks the numbers before sending the report.
example.zh: 她寄報告前一定會檢查數字。

example.en: Customers frequently ask about our return policy by email.
example.zh: 顧客經常用電子郵件詢問我們的退貨政策。

example.en: We regularly hold training sessions for new staff.
example.zh: 我們定期為新員工舉辦訓練。

example.en: I repeatedly asked for the invoice, but nobody replied.
example.zh: 我一再要求發票，但沒有人回覆。

derived.link: 詞幹；constant + -ly 變成副詞，像 quick → quickly、slow → slowly

extra_vocab.en: to try to reach a goal or do something over a long time
extra_vocab.note: 文章中的 pursue our goals 指努力追求自己的目標，是忙碌日常生活的一部分，語氣中性。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: pursue 是及物動詞，後面直接接目標，不加 for（✗ pursue for a goal）；名詞 pursuit 才搭配 in pursuit of。

example.en: She pursues new clients through phone calls and emails.
example.zh: 她透過電話和電子郵件開發新客戶。

example.en: He pursued a master's degree while working full time.
example.zh: 他一邊全職工作，一邊攻讀碩士學位。

example.en: We are pursuing a partnership with a Japanese supplier.
example.zh: 我們正在爭取與一家日本供應商合作。

example.en: It is easier to pursue a goal when everyone supports you.
example.zh: 有大家支持，追求目標會比較容易。

example.en: Many graduates want to pursue a career in marketing.
example.zh: 許多畢業生想從事行銷工作。

example.en: She decided to pursue a degree in finance at night.
example.zh: 她決定在夜間攻讀財務學位。

example.en: Our team will pursue this opportunity as soon as possible.
example.zh: 我們團隊會盡快爭取這個機會。

examples.en: The board decided to pursue a new strategy in Asia.
examples.zh: 董事會決定在亞洲採取新策略。

examples.en: Thank you for your complaint. We will pursue this matter right away.
examples.zh: 謝謝您的投訴，我們會立刻跟進處理此事。

examples.en: He left his job to pursue his dream of opening a café.
examples.zh: 他辭掉工作去追求開咖啡店的夢想。

confusable.diff: persuade 是「說服」，pursue 是「追求」，兩字拼法和開頭發音很像。
confusable.usage: persuade 常用 persuade + 人 + to V；pursue 後面直接接目標或事情。

example.en: She persuaded the manager to approve the budget.
example.zh: 她說服經理核准了預算。

similar.diff: seek 較正式，常接 help、advice、approval；pursue 強調持續努力去達成。

example.en: We seek advice from legal experts before signing contracts.
example.zh: 簽約前，我們會先向法律專家尋求意見。

similar.diff: go after 較口語，常用在主動去爭取客戶或機會。

example.en: Our sales team will go after the biggest clients first.
example.zh: 我們的業務團隊會先去爭取最大的客戶。

example.en: We achieved our sales goal two weeks early.
example.zh: 我們提前兩週達成了銷售目標。

example.en: The team accomplished a lot in just three months.
example.zh: 這個團隊在短短三個月內完成了很多事。

example.en: Our sales target for this quarter is very high.
example.zh: 我們這一季的銷售目標非常高。

derived.link: pursue 的結尾改成 -uit 變名詞，指「追求」這件事，常見於 in pursuit of（為了追求）

senses.en: to work for a goal over a long time

example.en: We pursue higher sales by offering better service.
example.zh: 我們藉由提供更好的服務來追求更高的銷售額。

senses.en: to study or work in a certain field
senses.distinguish: 受詞是職業、學位、研究時用這個意思。

example.en: Many nurses pursue further study while working at the hospital.
example.zh: 許多護理師一邊在醫院工作，一邊進修。

senses.en: to continue to deal with a problem or case
senses.distinguish: 受詞是投訴、案件、問題時用這個意思。

example.en: If the shop doesn't reply, the customer may pursue the complaint.
example.zh: 如果商店不回覆，顧客可能會繼續追究這項投訴。

extra_vocab.zh: 客觀地看待、從整體比例來看
extra_vocab.en: to think about how important something really is when you compare it with other things
extra_vocab.note: 例句中表示「放在整體裡比較，這個問題其實不大」，語氣是安慰與提醒；也呼應文章中 from the wrong perspective（看事情的角度）。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 受詞要放在 put 和 in perspective 中間（put it in perspective），不要說 put in perspective it；也常說 put things in perspective。

examples.en: Let's put this delay in perspective before we change the whole plan.
examples.zh: 在更改整個計畫之前，我們先客觀看待這次延誤。

examples.en: To put it in perspective, our costs rose only two percent.
examples.zh: 客觀來看，我們的成本只上升了百分之二。

examples.en: Her manager helped her put the mistake in perspective.
examples.zh: 她的經理幫助她客觀看待那個錯誤。

examples.en: Lost luggage is annoying, but let's put it in perspective.
examples.zh: 行李遺失很煩人，但我們還是客觀看待吧。

similar.diff: keep things in perspective 是持續保持客觀的狀態；put it in perspective 是把某件事拿來比較。

example.en: It is important to keep things in perspective during a busy season.
example.zh: 旺季期間，保持客觀的看法很重要。

similar.diff: look at the big picture 強調看整體、不被細節困住。

example.en: Let's look at the big picture before we cut the budget.
example.zh: 削減預算之前，我們先看整體狀況。

confusable.diff: prospective 是形容詞，指「未來可能的、潛在的」；perspective 是名詞，指看事情的角度。
confusable.usage: perspective 是名詞；prospective 是形容詞，放在名詞前，如 prospective clients。

example.en: We sent a brochure to every prospective client in Seoul.
example.zh: 我們寄了手冊給首爾每一位潛在客戶。

extra_vocab.en: belonging to each person or thing separately
extra_vocab.note: 這個字沒有直接出現在文章裡，但字尾和 perspective 相同，容易搞混。常用在 their respective + 複數名詞，表示每個人各有一份，多見於公司公告與會議。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: respective 只放在名詞前，常和 their 搭配，後面的名詞通常用複數（their respective roles）；不能放在 be 動詞後面當補語。

example.en: The two experts are famous in their respective fields.
example.zh: 這兩位專家在各自的領域都很有名。

example.en: Everyone should know their respective roles before the event starts.
example.zh: 活動開始前，每個人都應清楚自己的角色。

example.en: Please ask the respective departments to submit their budgets today.
example.zh: 請各部門今天提交各自的預算。

examples.en: Please send the reports to your respective managers by Friday.
examples.zh: 請在週五前把報告寄給你們各自的主管。

examples.en: Both teams will report their results to their respective supervisors.
examples.zh: 兩個團隊會各自向自己的主管報告結果。

examples.en: New employees will meet their respective team leaders on Monday.
examples.zh: 新進員工星期一會見各自的組長。

examples.en: The visitors returned to their respective hotels after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚餐後，訪客們各自回到自己的飯店。

examples.en: Each supplier will send a quote for its respective products.
examples.zh: 每家供應商會為自己的產品各自提出報價。

confusable.diff: respectful 是「有禮貌、尊重人的」；respective 是「各自的」，字根相同但意思差很多。
confusable.usage: respectful 描述人的態度，常接 of；respective 只放在名詞前，不描述人。

example.en: The staff are always respectful of customers' opinions.
example.zh: 員工總是尊重顧客的意見。

confusable.diff: perspective 是「看法、角度」，字尾和 respective 相同，容易搞混。
confusable.usage: perspective 是名詞（from a customer's perspective）；respective 是形容詞，放在名詞前。

example.en: From a customer's perspective, the website is hard to use.
example.zh: 從顧客的角度來看，這個網站很難用。

confusable.diff: respectively 是「分別地」，和 respective 同字根，但詞性不同。
confusable.usage: respectively 是副詞，放句尾，表示依序對應前面列出的項目。

example.en: Sales in May and June were $10,000 and $12,000, respectively.
example.zh: 五月和六月的銷售額分別是一萬和一萬兩千美元。

similar.diff: own 強調屬於自己；respective 強調每個人各有一份，語氣較正式。

example.en: Each team has its own budget for the project.
example.zh: 每個團隊都有自己的專案預算。

similar.diff: individual 強調一個一個分開看；respective 強調各自對應。

example.en: We reviewed each individual report before the meeting.
example.zh: 會議前，我們逐一檢查了每份報告。

example.en: Please send separate invoices for each order we placed.
example.zh: 請為我們下的每筆訂單分別寄發票。

example.en: Do you have a specific date for the meeting?
example.zh: 你有確定的會議日期嗎？

example.en: Please do not use the company phone for personal calls.
example.zh: 請不要用公司電話打私人電話。

derived.link: 詞幹；respect + -ive 變成 respective，像 active、creative 都是 -ive 形容詞
respective + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 quick → quickly
